Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like a period after a big policy rate cut, with a high unemployment rate relative to the last 36 months, weak payrolls, low inflation relative to its own history, and a very low policy rate. Gold is strongly up and the dollar is weak.

Candidate: mid-2020 to early 2021. Over a 36-month window, the unemployment z-score would be high, and the policy rate would be low (z of -2.0 versus a 2017-2020 average). But the 3m change in the policy rate of -1.0 doesn't fit mid-2020, since the cut was in March 2020. The unemployment 3m change of +1.5 is also at odds with that timing.

Another candidate: late 2025. Unemployment has been rising (4.1 to 4.4%), payrolls are weak, and the Fed has cut since September 2024. Gold is surging (+2.5 on 12m), and the dollar is down 12m. However, headline CPI at -0.5 versus the 3-year average (which includes 2023's 3-4%) fits, and core CPI at -1.0 fits too. The 2y yield at -1.5 and the 10y at -0.5 fit, giving a steep spread. The policy rate at -2.0 is odd given that it is still around 4%, but the 36-month window includes 5.3%, so this works only roughly. EM equity up 2.0 on 12m also fits 2025. VIX at 0 and a 1m equity return of -0.5 suggest a mild pullback, which matches November 2025. A 3m unemployment change of +1.5 fits too.

I'll go with November 2025.
